# Md Sabbir Ahmed Khan (Sabbir Khan, "Rey")

> Senior Android Engineer (also titled Senior Software Engineer) with 12+
> years of production Kotlin. He builds Android apps that sit inside larger
> systems: real-time telemetry over TCP, wearable sync over BLE, video
> pipelines with on-device computer vision, payments, and offline-first
> platforms for unreliable networks. Jetpack Compose, Coroutines and Flow,
> multi-module MVVM/MVI, Hilt, and Kotlin Multiplatform. He works with coding
> agents connected over MCP, and owns the architecture and the review of every
> line that ships.

Contact: rey.sabbir@gmail.com (the only public email address).
Website: https://reysabbir.com
CV, Senior Android Engineer (PDF): https://reysabbir.com/cv/Khan_Sabbir_CV_Senior_Android_Engineer.pdf
CV, Senior Software Engineer (PDF): https://reysabbir.com/cv/Khan_Sabbir_CV_Senior_Software_Engineer.pdf

## Who he is

- 12+ years shipping production software end to end, deepest in Android, plus
  the systems around the app: real-time telemetry, video pipelines, BLE sync,
  offline-first platforms.
- Founder of Power GP BD (2012–2018): 100+ Android apps shipped, two Facebook
  Startup Program awards. One app, Theatre, passed 500,000 Play Store downloads
  (it is no longer listed on the Play Store).
- At Kutumbita (2018–2019): designed and built Kinship.ai single-handedly, from
  architecture to Play Store release. A real-time workplace assistant putting HR
  self-service in the hands of garments-industry floor workers over Socket.io and
  Firebase Cloud Messaging (no longer listed on the Play Store).
- Lead Software Engineer II at Samsung R&D (2019–2022): Samsung Health, Wear OS
  companions syncing over BLE to Tizen watches, and feature work in the
  SmartThings iOS app.
- Led Android at Plentina (2022), a US fintech running Buy-Now-Pay-Later in the
  Philippines and Vietnam.
- At Avetics Global: owned the ground-up rewrite of two production Android apps,
  Volarious and V-Assist: multi-module architecture, Jetpack Compose, Hilt, and
  a real-time telemetry layer over custom TCP sockets, integrated with the DJI
  Mobile SDK. Set the architecture standards for a 6-person Android team.
- Selected by Google as a mentor for the Exchange with Google Developers pilot
  program (2021–2023); has trained 100+ developers across South and Southeast
  Asia, plus university and corporate teams.
- B.Sc. in Computer Science & Engineering, Ahsanullah University of Science and
  Technology.
- Languages: Bengali (native), English (professional).

## Core skills, by system layer

- **Mobile Engineering:** Kotlin · Jetpack Compose · Kotlin Multiplatform · Compose Multiplatform · Wear OS · Hilt · Room · WorkManager · iOS feature work (SmartThings)
- **System Architecture:** Multi-module clean architecture · MVVM & MVI · Coroutines & Flow · unidirectional state · Offline-first design · Background processing & sync
- **Connectivity & Protocols:** Custom TCP socket layers · BLE with retry-safe transfer · Socket.io real-time messaging · Firebase Cloud Messaging · Ktor · REST
- **Hardware & Device Integration:** DJI Mobile SDK · Tethered-drone systems · Tizen wearables · System overlays · Low-end device & network constraints
- **Media & Computer Vision:** Video codec & rendering pipelines · Live camera feeds · Real-time QR detection & tracking · Latency budgeting
- **Backend & Cloud:** Firebase Auth & Realtime Database · Payment gateway integration · Backend API integration · Google Play release engineering
- **AI-Assisted Engineering:** Claude Code · Codex · Gemini CLI · Cursor · MCP-connected workflows (Jira, Figma, GitHub, Firebase) · Agent-driven delivery under senior review

## Case studies

- **Volarious & V-Assist — Real-Time Aircraft Control from Android** (Avetics Global): Two Android products for Avetics Global, running side by side on the same rugged tablet: Volarious, the operator’s control app, and V-Assist, the companion for tethered-power operations. Between them it is the brief any serious Android app carries — authentication, a live telemetry dashboard, light and dark themes, device settings, a system overlay, error and recovery states, Play Store releases — with one twist that shapes every decision: the data arriving over the socket is a live aircraft, so late data is useless data.
  Role: Senior Android Engineer. I owned the ground-up architectural rewrite, built features across both apps, and set the engineering standards the 6-person Android team worked to.
  V-Assist on Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.volarious.vlinestatus
  https://reysabbir.com/projects/#avetics
- **Plentina — Buy Now, Pay Later** (GrowFolio (formerly Plentina), Feb 2022 – Nov 2022 · Remote (US)): A US fintech startup expanding BNPL credit access across the Philippines and Vietnam needed its Android app to move fast in two markets — with payment flows that simply cannot fail.
  Role: Led Android development of the Plentina BNPL app.
  https://reysabbir.com/projects/#plentina
- **Samsung Health & WearOS** (Samsung R&D Institute, Oct 2019 – Feb 2022 · Dhaka): Samsung’s consumer health ecosystem spans phones, wearables and servers. Health data has to stay consistent across all three — including watches running a completely different OS (Tizen).
  Role: Lead Software Engineer II. I built health-tracking Android applications and their WearOS companions inside Samsung’s consumer wellness product line, and contributed features to the SmartThings iOS app.
  https://reysabbir.com/projects/#samsung
- **Kinship.ai — Workplace Assistant for the Factory Floor** (Kutumbita, 2018 – 2019): Bangladesh’s garments industry employs hundreds of thousands of floor workers whose only route to HR is a queue and a paper form. Kinship.ai replaced it with a chat thread: ask the assistant a question, report a broken machine with a photo, apply for leave, check salary or attendance — in the moment, on the cheap Android phone already in their pocket.
  Role: I designed and built the Android app entirely on my own — architecture, implementation and Play Store release.
  https://reysabbir.com/projects/#kinship

## Public projects

- **Football Predictor 2026** — The bracket engine for FIFA’s new 48-team World Cup. FIFA’s 2026 format is new and genuinely hard: 48 teams, 12 groups, and a Round of 32 where third-placed qualifiers depend on results across every other group. I designed an engine that evaluates 450+ valid bracket combinations and recalculates the entire knockout tree in real time as you fill in results — following the official FIFA regulations to the letter. What takes analysts spreadsheets, the app does instantly, 100% offline.
  Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=xyz.androidrey.predictor
- **Study Quran** — An online-class marketplace, built for Android from zero to Play Store. I built the complete Android app for an early-stage startup in two months. Students sign in with Google, browse a marketplace of teachers, book live classes, start a free trial and pay securely. The startup’s own team owned the backend APIs and the admin panel, and I integrated the app against them.
  Study Quran on Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=live.studyquran.android
- **GitHub Client** — The “how I write code” exhibit — read the source. An open-source Android app I keep public for one reason: so you can see exactly how I structure production code. Multi-module clean architecture (app / features / common / network / storage / theme), unidirectional state, offline support, and real tests — not a toy repo.
  Source on GitHub: https://github.com/sabbirreyjohn/Github-Client · YouTube demo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pzxTVq5kKnE

## Answers to the questions he is usually asked

### Walk me through a hard problem you solved recently.

On V-Assist, I owned a premium feature the company had already marketed. The drone scans a QR code from the air, tracks it in flight, and lands precisely on top of it, from the Android-based DJI remote control.

Close to release, it was failing. At high image quality, QR scanning lagged behind the live feed, so the drone couldn’t follow the code in time to land. The easy fix was to drop the image quality and ship. Instead I debugged the pipeline line by line, and the real bottleneck turned out to be the video codec and rendering path. Detection was fine.

Working from the codec documentation, I rebalanced decoding and rendering so the feed kept its quality while scanning ran in real time. The feature shipped on schedule, the drone lands on the mark without crashing, and it’s live in production today. I try to work that way in general: find the actual cause before trading away part of the product.

### What work are you proudest of?

The one closest to my heart is Theatre, a multimedia app from my Power GP BD years that crossed 500,000 downloads on the Play Store (it’s no longer live). Half a million people chose something I built, and I still think about that.

The most recent one is Football Predictor 2026. FIFA’s new 48-team format is algorithmically nasty: the Round of 32 depends on third-place results across all 12 groups, with 450+ valid bracket combinations. I built an engine that resolves the whole knockout tree in real time, by the letter of the FIFA regulations. It turned something that confuses everyone into something anyone can play with.

### What do you bring to a team?

I translate. I can sit with product managers, designers and stakeholders, work out what they actually need, and turn it into technical decisions. After twelve years of shipping end to end, I do more than write the code: I design the architecture, build it, release it and keep it running.

I also automate repetitive work instead of putting up with it, and I stay calm when a deadline gets tight. I would rather find the smart fix than pull an all-nighter. Ask my last three teams about release week.

### You use AI heavily. How do you keep the engineering rigorous?

I make the decisions and the agents do the typing. Architecture, tech stack and library choices are mine. The agents speed up the implementation, but I keep track of what they use, steer them off the wrong library and onto the right one, and shape the code so it holds up later with fewer bugs.

I keep up with the tooling so I can direct it well. Every line that ships is one I have reviewed and can defend.

### What kind of work do you do best?

Android is my deepest stack, and the work I enjoy most puts it inside a larger system: hardware, real-time data, sync across devices, payments. That is where architecture decisions really matter.

The common thread is ownership. I do my best work when I am accountable for the outcome, not just the ticket, and when I can build something I am willing to stand behind.
